title: Victory Red Day
description:
A campaign for a Day of Female Solidarity and Empowerment on June 24, 2025—the anniversary of Roe v. Wade’s repeal. The idea is simple yet powerful: women and supporters of women everywhere wear red lipstick as a symbol of strength, resilience, and the ongoing fight for gender equality.

Victory Red lipstick has long been a symbol of women’s power, particularly during World War II, when it was worn by women on the home front to represent strength, defiance, and patriotism. During this time, women stepped into roles previously held by men, contributing to the war effort while asserting their independence and resilience. They stood against facism, all while maintaining households and duties outside of their normal realm.

title: "Moral Monday" Street Rally

address_lines: N. Main St. and W. Division St.

description:
Please join us in opposing cuts to essential safety net programs!

Please join us at weekly recurring  "Moral Monday" street rallies, alternating between Hudson WI and River Falls WI.

Our first “Moral Monday” street rally will be in Downtown Hudson on Monday May 5, from 4PM to 6PM, at the intersection of Second and Vine Streets, where we will hold signs and stand along the public sidewalks.

Our second “Moral Monday” street rally will be in River Falls on Monday May 12, from 4PM to 6PM, at the intersection of Main and Division Streets, where we will hold signs and stand along the public sidewalks.

Folks may join for part or all the two hours, and may bring their own signs or use signs we’ll have to share.

If the weather is bad—hard rain, high wind, and/or lightening—we’ll cancel that week’s rally.

Our "Moral Monday" street rallies are inspired and informed by work of the prominent North Carolina pastor and anti-poverty activist the Rev. William Barber, who founded the Center for Public Theology and Public Policy at Yale and now teaches there.

On the twelfth anniversary of his first "Moral Monday" demonstration, Monday April 28, 2025, Rev. Barber was arrested for praying against the Republican-led budget while in the Rotunda of our US Capitol. At a rally held before he entered the Rotunda to pray, Rev. Barber said: “Forty-three percent of women and almost half of all children are poor and low income. Somebody ought to say something … Somebody gotta challenge this budget.”

We are holding "Moral Monday" street rallies to voice our challenges.

We oppose Republican-approved Congressional budget resolutions that harm the poorest and most vulnerable of Americans in order to give more than $5-trillion in tax breaks to the richest and most privileged of Americans.

We oppose Trump/Musk budget proposals that eliminate or make draconian cuts to federal programs for child care, health research, education, housing assistance, community development, and the elderly.

These funding cuts and proposed budgets are not just public policy choices, they are moral choices. 

These funding cuts and proposed budgets are morally wrong, not just bad public policy choices. 

Please join with us to "say something" and "challenge this budget".

title: Croton, NY: Pass a Resolution Against Project Maple
description:
**Join us outside the Croton Board of Trustees meeting to demand local action against Project Maple** — a dangerous fracked gas pipeline expansion plan that threatens our climate, our river, and our health.

Fossil Fuel company Enbridge's Project Maple would expand the amount of fracked gas running through the existing Algonquin Pipeline (which runs through Westchester County) by replacing existing pipe and expanding compressor stations. 

This project would lock us into decades of fossil fuel dependence — just when we need to be transitioning to clean energy. It’s risky, unnecessary, and completely out of step with New York’s climate goals. **Croton has the chance to be a climate leader by passing a resolution opposing this reckless project.**

Meet us outside Croton-on-Hudson Village Hall, where we’ll rally together, then head into the board meeting to make powerful public comments demanding the Village take a stand.

Let’s pack the room and show our elected officials that Croton stands for climate justice, not fossil fuel expansion. Bring your friends, your voice, and your passion — we’ll have talking points and signs ready to go!

title: 12 Days to Democracy! JOIN THE MARCH - June 16 to 28
description:
Democracy has always been about the power of the people. It’s we, the people, who will fight the fight for a more just and equitable society.

This is the work– not of kings– but by all of us and for all of us. We’re the ones who have to travel the distance.

And this is why, at this critical juncture in our history - when the laws and institutions protecting our right to fight are under attack like never before - we have decided to take a very long walk.

Our walk – a 120-mile journey from Philly to DC - will take us through towns, into cities, and along the trails of the East Coast Greenway, and we hope that it will look like the world we want to see: friendly and civil. Open to the joys of human variation and the friendliness of flexible minds. This is a big, long mission; a walk/march, inspired by the big, hopeful, goodness-based, law-governed dream that is American democracy. We hope you’ll consider joining us - for a mile, a city limit, the whole journey.

FOR MORE DETAILS VISIT OUR WEBSITE: https://www.democracy12.com/

TO LEARN MORE, TO MEET THE ORGANIZERS OR TO LEARN HOW YOU CAN HELP THE EFFORT, ATTEND A ZOOM MEETING: https://mobilize.us/s/hXiRHp

Note: Mobilize does not allow for multi-day events. We will reach out to you to obtain information on how you will be participating. 


*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Sound the Alarm for Democracy

location.venue: Vigo County Annex Building of Terre Haute

description:
***If you are not from Terre Haute, Please start one of these near you! We would love this to be Nationwide!!!***

The Trump Administration and Elon Musk are acting with selfishness, hiding their actions in cowardice, and systematically dismantling the values upon which our country was built. The speed of the destruction has been truly horrific, and we the people are alarmed at the state of our democracy! So Indivisible Wabash Valley has launched the "Sound the Alarm for Democracy" weekly event. 

Every Monday at 12:05 pm, sound the panic on your car alarms, honk your horns, bang a drum, blow a trumpet, sing the Star Spangled Banner, or make noise however you can. The idea is that anyone can participate, no matter where they are, no matter what they are doing.

Those who are able will meet at the Vigo County Annex each week, everyone else, just make noise wherever you are: homes, schools, churches, jobs! We want to let our neighbors, our elected officials, and the rest of the world know that a lot of us are out here, still standing together to protect our democracy, and the rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness, fought for and defended for 250 years and counting.

JOIN US EVERY MONDAY!!
SOUND THE ALARM FOR DEMOCRACY

title: We The People Wednesdays in Walnut Creek
description:
This is a local Indivisible event organized by Indivisible ReSisters Contra Costa!  Join us every Wednesday evening from 5-6 p.m. at the corner of Ygnacio Valley Road and Civic Drive for a rousing honk and wave visibility action.  Bring your signs and raise your voice for democracy and to protect our rights!  

This is a nonviolent event. Stay within your rights, don’t break laws, stay safe, stay peaceful, and avoid any risk you don’t feel comfortable with. Don’t obstruct traffic, impede pedestrians, or commit any acts of property damage. If counterprotestors appear, do your best to ignore them.  When people shout from cars, just remember that we are standing for their rights, too.  They just don't know it.

This is a busy intersection and cars drive fast.  Please stay on the sidewalk at least a few feet from cars.  We can spread out down the block and take a stand on the pedestrian overpass.  Safety is our top priority.  If you have any concerns during this event, please find a peace ambassador in an orange vest and they will help.

There are several parking lots within walking distance or you can find street parking at Civic Park or on Civic Drive or Arroyo Way.

title: Paramus Tesla Takedown
description:
It looks like Musk is officially out of the White House — for now. But that doesn’t let him off the hook for the damage he’s done or the chaos he’s still capable of causing. Our institutions are weakened and in disarray. He holds troves of our data. He’s linked to the deaths of thousands of the world’s poorest children. And you can bet he’ll use his billions to influence future elections.

Now is the time to double down — not back off. #TeslaTakedown put it best:

"𝘞𝘦 𝘩𝘢𝘷𝘦 𝘌𝘭𝘰𝘯 𝘰𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘳𝘰𝘱𝘦𝘴. 𝘞𝘦 𝘤𝘢𝘯'𝘵 𝘭𝘦𝘵 𝘶𝘱 𝘯𝘰𝘸. 𝘏𝘦'𝘴 𝘴𝘵𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘳𝘪𝘤𝘩𝘦𝘴𝘵 𝘮𝘢𝘯 𝘪𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘭𝘥. 𝘏𝘦 𝘴𝘵𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘸𝘪𝘦𝘭𝘥𝘴 𝘦𝘯𝘰𝘳𝘮𝘰𝘶𝘴 𝘱𝘰𝘸𝘦𝘳. 𝘏𝘦 𝘪𝘴 𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘱𝘰𝘯𝘴𝘪𝘣𝘭𝘦 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘮𝘢𝘴𝘴 𝘴𝘶𝘧𝘧𝘦𝘳𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘥𝘦𝘢𝘵𝘩. 𝘈𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘤𝘢𝘶𝘴𝘦 𝘮𝘰𝘳𝘦 𝘪𝘧 𝘸𝘦 𝘨𝘪𝘷𝘦 𝘩𝘪𝘮 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘤𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘵𝘰 𝘳𝘦𝘤𝘰𝘷𝘦𝘳 𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘳𝘦𝘱𝘶𝘵𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯.

𝘈𝘧𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘦 2020 𝘦𝘭𝘦𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘑𝘢𝘯𝘶𝘢𝘳𝘺 6, 𝘢 𝘭𝘰𝘵 𝘰𝘧 𝘱𝘦𝘰𝘱𝘭𝘦 𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘷𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘦𝘥 𝘋𝘰𝘯𝘢𝘭𝘥 𝘛𝘳𝘶𝘮𝘱 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘵𝘰𝘢𝘴𝘵. 𝘈 𝘭𝘰𝘵 𝘰𝘧 𝘧𝘰𝘭𝘬𝘴 𝘴𝘢𝘪𝘥 "𝘓𝘰𝘰𝘬 𝘧𝘰𝘳𝘸𝘢𝘳𝘥, 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘣𝘢𝘤𝘬𝘸𝘢𝘳𝘥," 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘯𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘳 𝘩𝘦𝘭𝘥 𝘢𝘤𝘤𝘰𝘶𝘯𝘵𝘢𝘣𝘭𝘦. 𝘓𝘦𝘵'𝘴 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘮𝘢𝘬𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘬𝘦 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘌𝘭𝘰𝘯."

⚡Sell your Teslas, dump your stock, join the picket lines.

⚡ We're tanking Tesla's stock price to stop Musk.

⚡Stopping Musk will help save lives and protect our democracy.

The stakes couldn’t be higher. No one is coming to save us. Not politicians, not the media, not the courts.

Tesla Takedown is a peaceful protest movement. We oppose violence, vandalism and destruction of property. This protest is a lawful exercise of our First Amendment right to peaceful assembly.

#TeslaTakedown #BoycottTesla

title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ Moon Valley in North Central Phoenix
description:

Every Wednesday, @ 7:30 am, we'll gather at Serafina Coffee Roasters on 7th St & Coral Gables to grab a beverage, walk across the parking lot to the sidewalk, and show the busy morning commuters that they are not alone.

Peak traffic time seems to be from 7:45 to 8:30a. Yes, it's already hot in Phoenix, so plan accordingly. 

Spread the word. Come join us. Or start your own!

All the details you need are at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

Love this idea and [want to start your own Rush-hour Resistance Rally in your area](https://rhrr.us/#start-your-own)? Groovy! Let's make that happen!

title: Protest to Support our LGBTQ+ Community
description:
This a local Indivisible event!
Protest to Support our LGBTQ+ Community

Date: Sunday, June 22nd 
Time: 4:00PM-5:30PM
Location: Hyannis Airport Rotary (details about parking and where exactly to stand listed below.) 
Please wear “pride spirit” to make a visual impact as a rainbow sea of love, acceptance, and appreciation for diversity and all the unique talents that makes our community so vibrant. 
As always, please bring signs, flags, drums, other instruments, chants, art, etc., as joy is resistance, art is resistance, community is resistance. [Joyful community resistance to fascism]

In honor/celebration of pride month, we are protesting against Trump & his administration, specifically against the harm he has caused to the LGBTQ+ community. We are infuriated with his executive orders that ban gender affirming care for minors, that restrict trans rights, and that eliminate protections against discrimination for those in the LGBTQ+ community. We recognize the detrimental effect this has had on the well being of many individuals and the community as a whole. We stand in solidarity to say we will not put up with this.
We will not allow this administration’s attacks on the LGBTQ+ community to continue! #RESIST
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

******Corruption destroys, Community Builds: We will also be collecting nonperishable food items for the AIDS support group in Hyannis. ******

We are being cosponsored by a local pride group, and have invited local pride groups to set up informational tables if they are available. 

As with every protest, we also want to highlight the extreme unconstitutional practices of this administration, as this is not just about policies. 
This is NOT business as usual in DC, this is NOT normal. 

This republican administration has attempted to seize control over state election processes through executive orders and efforts to undermine civil rights legislation, as well as threatening the checks and balances established by the Constitution, such as disregarding court orders and altering federal regulations without proper authority.​​ The administration is using its current power to help billionaires continue to profit while striping away the services that help the most needy. 

We need to stand up for due process, free speech, upholding court rulings, and the separation of church and state. The Founding Fathers established the principles of due process, free speech, and the separation of church and state through the First Amendment and other parts of the Constitution. These concepts were designed to protect individual rights and limit government power. 
We have NO KINGS in America, yet Trump is acting like one. 
We, the people, must rise up, and show that the power of the people is greater than the people in power. 

Protest Homework (aka, protest action steps)
5 Calls App or Website, National Action Steps:
Scroll down to the LGBTQ+ section, as of right now there are 2 calls to make (to all 3 of your members of congress!):
1. *“condemn RFK Jr’s False Report on Transgender Youth Treatment” and 
2. *“Oppose Efforts to Dehumanize transgender and LGBTQ+ people” 
If you have time for another round of calls, please scroll to “executive overreach” and click:
3. *”fight the trump administration’s defiance of the constitution and courts”

We The People stand to:

•Save the Constitution •Save Medicare •Save Medicaid •Save Social Security •Save Veteran’s Services •Save funding to universities and non-profits •Save the Department of Education •Save EPA •Save NOAA •Save libraries •Save Head Start •Stop ICE from kidnapping people •Stop attacks on free speech •Stop the othering of the queer/transgender community

title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ ICE Field Office in Phoenix
description:
Big events with thousands of people are great. But we also need local, more frequent rallies that show locals that they're not alone in this fight.

**When we realized the DHS/ICE field office is in our neighborhood, we decided it would be the perfect place for an ICE-specific RhRR!**

Every Thursday @ 7:00 am, we'll gather on the south east corner of Central and Monte Vista, right in front of the ICE Field office.

**STAY ON THE SIDEWALK!** It's public property and we've a right to be there. Be sure you **DO NOT BLOCK** access to the building—that means cars as well as people.

**Please make ICE-specific signs**, as we're here to show the busy morning commuters that they are not alone and the ICE staffers that We The People care about due process for everyone.

Spread the word. Come join us. All the details you need are at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us/#museum-district).

Love this idea and want to start your own Rush-hour Resistance Rally in your area? Groovy! [Let's make that happen!](https://rhrr.us/#start-your-own)

Join us on July 5th for a peaceful march and rally to reaffirm our commitment to democratic principles and stand against the threats of autocracy. As we gather just after Independence Day, we honor our founders' revolutionary spirit and their rejection of monarchical rule.

Why July 5th?

While the nation celebrates on the 4th, we gather the day after to remind ourselves that independence isn't just a historical achievement—it's an ongoing responsibility. Just as the revolutionaries of 1776 declared "No More Kings," we continue their legacy by standing vigilant against autocratic tendencies in our own time.

What to Bring:

- Signs (suggested themes: democratic values, checks and balances, "No Kings Since 1776")
- Water and sun protection
- Your commitment to peaceful democratic action

This non-partisan event welcomes all who believe in preserving democratic institutions and opposing autocratic governance, regardless of political affiliation.

title: Protest Elon Musk's Illegal Government Takeover #TeslaTakedown - Stanford Saturdays
description:
PLEASE READ COMPLETELY before attending!

This is a peaceful, nonviolent protest on the sidewalk in front of the Stanford Tesla showroom. There will be theatrics and dancing. Get ready to improv! We'll also be looping through Stanford Shopping Mall with peaceful positive energy. Of course you may opt out and continue to demonstrate in front of the Tesla showroom. 

We know making lots of noise is typically part of a good protest. But most protests aren’t right across the street from a Ronald McDonald House. Let’s take care to keep our noise levels down to a dull roar. Bring your energy and spirit, but let’s refrain from the cowbells, drums and car honks. We can get our point across without interfering with our neighbors on the other side of the road.

Wear your favorite wig, big hat, or costume. We want to have fun and to feel like a party during our demonstrations! Signs, flags, and similar items are welcome.

This is a peaceful demonstration, and any conflicts or altercations will not be tolerated. Walk away if one arises and report it to the demonstration leader on site if it is a serious altercation. We will comply with requests from the police and mall security, including if we are asked to leave. By the way, we have already have a fantastic relationship with mall security, which is a plus!

Do not boo or confront Tesla drivers or cars, or Tesla employees. Remember that most Tesla drivers are our allies, and many are protesting with us!

Please Note: Photos may be taken and published at this event, including by attendees and professional photographers. If you prefer not to have your image captured or shared, please take your own precautions (e.g., wear a mask, hat, or wig).

#BoycottTesla #DivestFromTesla

description:
**Join The Salmonberry Trail in our exciting ground breaking event at Waterfront Park in Wheeler!**

The City of Wheeler is excited to announce that we are taking the first steps toward revitalization of Wheeler’s section of the Salmonberry Trail through partnership with the Salmonberry Trail Foundation and Tillamook Coast Visitors Association. We will be holding a **Ground Building event and ceremony on July 12, 2025 from 1:00-5:00 PM.** We truly could not be more excited for the recreational opportunities this trail will provide for our community.

This transformative project holds the potential to deliver lasting, meaningful benefits to our community. By linking the Willamette Valley to the Coast, it will not only strengthen regional connectivity but also invigorate rural tourism and empower small businesses. It champions public health and safe, active transportation options while expanding equitable access to the outdoors for all residents. Most importantly, it lays the foundation for sustainable infrastructure that will support our economy, environment, and quality of life for generations to come.

We will have local vendors, music, games, and a ribbon cutting ceremony celebrating the beginning of this coastal section of the trail. 
- July 12th, 1PM - 5PM
- Waterfront Park (500 Marine Dr, Wheeler, OR 97147)

---
**ABOUT THE SALMONBERRY TRAIL**
The Salmonberry Trail is an 82-mile multi-use path transforming a historic rail line into Oregon’s next big adventure. Connecting communities from the Willamette Valley to the coast, the trail will provide safe routes for recreation and education, expand economic opportunities, and improve public health. In partnership with local organizations, it will offer unique educational programs while promoting outdoor activity and conservation, making it a cornerstone of community development and environmental stewardship across the state.

**Wheeler Demonstration Project – Salmonberry Trail**
The Wheeler Demonstration Project is a short, high-impact segment of the Salmonberry Trail located in downtown Wheeler. This 1,800-foot trail segment runs north from Rector Street, across Hemlock Street, and along the bay side of the Oregon Coast Scenic Railway tracks adjacent to Botts Marsh. It features a compacted gravel path for pedestrians, designed to enhance safety and encourage walking in the downtown area.
Developed in partnership with the City of Wheeler, Oregon Coast Scenic Railway, Lower Nehalem Community Trust, and the Salmonberry Trail Foundation, the project supports local economic activity, offers environmental education through interpretive signage, and provides a model for similar efforts in other communities along the trail corridor.

description:
**Come to the Orange Plaza Square Park each week**, rain or shine, to take a stand opposing the oligarchs, billionaires and the regime that's attacking our way of life and the Constitution of the USA. Join our community in a nonviolent, peaceful demonstration! Make your voice heard. We are the many, they are the few that want to rule us all. Take a stand for democracy. Bring your signs, bring pots and pans, your whistles and kazoos and meet at the fountain - we'll spread out from there after a safety briefing. Let the people be heard! Let’s make some noise!

**GENERAL PROTEST/RALLY REMINDERS**

Remember the ABCs of protesting:

A) Always obey traffic signals and directions of the safety team!

B) Beware of detractors*! Do not talk to detractors or unaffiliated interviewers - doing so increases risks for all of us, including all the volunteers and organizers.

C) Chill vibes please! Never touch anyone else or their property (e.g., car, sign, backpack) without permission. Have fun! Build community!

*As our events become more popular, we may attract detractors and Trump/Elon/MAGA supporters, either passing in cars or as rally attendees. Some of their tactics are to act friendly, ask questions, and pretend to care about your answers. They may also gesture, yell, name-call, and use foul language. They often look to get a reaction they can capture on video. Do NOT engage with or speak to them. Do NOT answer their questions. Do NOT yell back at them or gesture (thumbs down, middle finger, etc.) Do NOT post photos or videos of them online. Do NOT reveal any personal or contact info to anyone at this or any rally you do not know to be on your side. If someone becomes threatening or violent, move away quickly and alert a safety volunteer, a police officer, and/or call 911. These guidelines keep you, our volunteers, and our organizers safe. Thank you!

**[Learn to de-escalate](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Pgmn9QRr48&list=PLqIrQkVlKU3RZw0ytVd3U7XS3ofAaZItu&index=2)**

**[Learn to Grey-rock](https://health.clevelandclinic.org/grey-rock-method)**

**MEET YOUR HOST**

**[Indivisible CA 40](https://linktr.ee/indivisibleca40)** is a non-partisan, all volunteer grassroots group of residents in the CA-40 congressional district who are holding elected officials accountable, from city councils and school boards all the way up to Congress. title: The Roadmap for Winning: A Conversation with Adam Kinzinger and North Texas Local Election Winners
description:
Join us for Roadmap to Winning, a powerful gathering to celebrate how we beat back MAGA extremism—not with more money, but with more heart, more truth, and the will of the people. 

This event is more than a victory lap—it’s a strategy session for the future. We turned the tide in 2025. Now, we build the momentum to turn this first blue wave into a tidal wave in 2026. Learn from the organizers, leaders, and everyday heroes who made it happen—and how we do it again, bigger and bolder.

Together, we map the road ahead. Let’s keep fighting. Let’s keep winning.

**Featured Guest: Adam Kinzinger**

Adam Kinzinger is a former Republican congressman from Illinois and U.S. Air Force veteran known for his outspoken opposition to MAGA extremism. A key member of the January 6th Committee, he prioritized truth and accountability over party loyalty. After leaving Congress, he founded Country First to promote democracy and combat political division.

_**Panelists:**_

**Dr. John Biggan: HEB ISD Trustee**

Dr. John Biggan is a cognitive neuroscientist and data scientist who works in the child welfare system, using research and data to improve the lives of the children in this community, the state, and nationwide. A longtime Hurst resident and advocate for public education, he brings a research-driven approach to his role on the HEB ISD Board of Trustees, focusing on student success, teacher support, and fiscal responsibility.

**Vanessa Pacheco: Richardson ISD Trustee**

Vanessa Pacheco, single-member district 2; elected in June 2022. Mrs. Pacheco is the Chief Operations Officer for Carrolton Injury Law. She and her husband, Jorge, have a daughter who graduated from Berkner High School in 2020 and a son who graduated from Richardson High School in 2023.

**Amir Omar: Richardson Mayor**

Amir Omar is believed to be the first Muslim elected to political office in North Texas. Omar was elected to the Richardson City Council, Place 7 in May 2009, defeating incumbent Dennis Stewart by 51.54% to 48.46%. On May 3, 2025, Omar defeated incumbent Bob Dubey 54.4% to 41.6% in the mayoral race.

**Laney Hawes: Texas Freedom to Read Project and, Keller ISD Families for Public Education; Co-Founder**

Laney Hawes is the Co-Founder of the Texas Freedom to Read Project and the hyper local organization, Keller ISD Families for Public Education.  She's passionate about true grassroots activism, public education, and the freedom to read. Laney resides in North Fort Worth with her husband and four children.

**Adam Bazaldua: Dallas City Councilman**

Deputy Mayor Pro Tem Bazaldua is the youngest elected Council Member to the City of Dallas in its current form of government.Bazaldua is a dedicated father and husband who has been a chef and a teacher. For the last five years, Council Member Adam Bazaldua has served as the City Council Member for Dallas' City Council District 7.

For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:
General Visibility Rules:
•	Distance is Key: The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
•	"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility: A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
•	Bridge Specifics: Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.
Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:
•	Go Big: Aim for lettering that is at least 12-24 inches tall, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
•	Bold, Simple Fonts: Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
•	High Contrast Colors: This is critical!
o	Dark letters on a light background (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
o	Avoid low-contrast combinations like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
o	Limit your color palette to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
•	Concise Messaging: Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
•	Material and Construction:
o	Sturdy materials: Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
o	Weatherproof: Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
o	Double-sided signs: If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
•	Test Your Signs: Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
•	Spacing (Kerning): Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.
By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: Weekly (Fri) Mass Pike Overpass Standout in Westfield - Southampton Rd (Routes 10/202)
description:
Wow! What a great location for a standout! On 5/30, around 17 people, including a bagpiper!  What a blast! LOTS of engagement with motorists!

There's lots and lots of traffic passing by. Southampton Road (Routes 10/202) is heavily traveled northbound and southbound, and the Mass Pike eastbound and westbound is below. Lots of honks and thumbs up and waves...and a few folks flying middle fingers. We smile and wave at them all! 

We'll have letterboards prepared for the lower part of the overpass fencing - the photo shows how that will look to folks passing on the Mass Pike. We're interacting with motorists on the Mass Pike, and on Southampton Road. We've discovered that the magic happens when we smile and wave to people!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire 1 1/2 hours.

### How to Get There

The address "130 Southampton Road, Westfield" will get you just north of the overpass. 

### Parking

We can't park in the Southampton Rd breakdown lane. There are vacant business properties north of the bridge, and it seems that parking would be OK there.

It looks like The Wealth Technology Group has vacated their office at 130 Southampton Rd, but the internet says that other businesses are located there, so please be mindful if you decide to park there.

### Etiquette!

We don't give the finger to people who give the finger to us, or who say unpleasant things. We smile and wave to them, too. 

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

And, if you have an extra 3' x 5' American flag you're not using, we'd love it if you'd pass it on to us!

description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Mark your calendars! Bring the kids! Join us on June 21st @ 10:30am for our March to the Park! from the Tuscarawas Co Courthouse to Tuscora Park (one mile). Join us afterwards for a potluck. Together with the League of Women Voters Tuscarawas County, we are collecting monetary donations for Jack’s House of Hope. 

Departure time: 10:45am! Bring your own signs to this event.

Signs

For this event, please bring your own signs. They can be on wood sticks such as tomatoe posts for ease of carrying. Make your message clear: Federal, state, and local issues of concern to you, your family, the community…there are just so many issues my head would explode if I wrote them all down. Pre-made signs will not be available for this event.

Monetary Donations

Together with the League of Women Voters of Tusc County, we are asking marchers to make a monetary donation of any amount for Jack’s House of Hope. Monetary donations for Jack’s House of Hope will be collected at Tuscora Park. Amanda Fontana, Friends of the Homeless of Tuscarawas County Board of Directors' Secretary will speak about the importance of our local shelter.

March, Eat, Chat, Play!

Our event is from 10:30am-12:30pm. We will march to Tuscora Park from the Tuscarawas County Courthouse and then share a covered dish and/or just bring something for yourself/your family, your own paper products/utensils, snacks to share, and good conversation with those joining us. If you bring something to share, please be mindful of allergies. An index card with a list of ingredients taped to the container would be appreciated. Label containers with your name if you want them back! Jenn Schrock will oversee the food/refreshments while we march.

Half of a covered pavilion near the bocce courts has been reserved for this event. Blankets and chairs can be dropped off beforehand. Marchers can carpool back to the Tusc Co Courthouse to then walk to the park (10:45am). For those that do not have a way back to the courthouse to march, Alicia Hall will help transport people to the courthouse BEFORE the march once they drop off their items at the park.

Remember: Bring your own signs to this event!

Kids can play on the playground equipment. Park rides and Putt-Putt golf open at NOON. See pricing at www.tuscorapark.com/park-info-contact.

We’ll take a group picture!

Helpers

We need helpers at the park to remain with the food, etc. until the marchers arrive. We also need help along the route, guiding marchers as they cross side streets. We don’t block traffic, we hold marchers on the sidewalk while traffic makes their turn left or right onto North Broadway. Let us know if you’re interested in helping.

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._

title: Weekly Darrell Issa Office Rallies!
description:
Join us every Friday from 10:30 at Darrell Issa’s Escondido office. We’ll meet first at the office and then walk as a group to the public sidewalk on Lincoln Blvd. Bring your protest signs and a folding chair if you can’t stand for an hour or so. Consider a double-sided sign so that you can have one message for Issa and another for the motorists.

HANDS OFF: Our bodies Our healthcare Our public lands Our education Our human rights

Rallies are a great way to meet other like-minded community members. They remind us that we aren’t alone and it feels good to be civically engaged. Action is the antidote to despair. We guarantee you will feel better about the state of affairs when you leave this event.

Please note that there is a mental health services business in Issa’s office. Please allow a direct path the elevator for patients at all times. Refrain from banging on the glass doors as it has been reported to upset some of the patients. Please follow all posted rules and traffic laws when attending a rally. Safety is always our first priority. Safety patrol volunteers will be wearing bright vests - please comply with their requests at all times.

title: GOOD TROUBLE LIVES ON: Williamsburg, VA
description:
ALL OUR ACTIONS WILL BE PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE!!!

Our rights are under attack. Our democracy is under siege. We’ve been here before, and we know what to do.

On July 17, we honor the anniversary of the passing of civil rights hero John Lewis, not with ceremonies, but with action. Across the country, we will take to the streets, courthouses, and community spaces to carry forward his fight for justice, voting rights, and dignity for all.

This is more than a protest, it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

**Please note:** a core principle behind our John Lewis Good Trouble Day actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

This is more than a protest, it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

COMMUNITY NORMS:

Please read before attending one of our events.

One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS. Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day”.

At our events, please do not hold signs or otherwise promote other events that Williamsburg JCC Indivisible is not hosting. You may be placing a potential legal liability onto our group that we are NOT willing to accept.

Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS! If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, cowbells, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave!

As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers. At larger events, these organizers will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirts with yellow safety vests. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk. We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

No Kings — We reject authoritarianism, elite rule, and leaders who place themselves above the people.

Come stand in solidarity with your community as we protest outside of Texas State Senator Angela Paxton's office in Allen, TX. We demand representation and we will fight to repeal these harmful measures!

title: Avelo Airline Nationwide Protest
description:
**Indivisible Mesa is joining the Coalition to Stop Avelo's nationwide call to action for a full boycott of Avelo Airlines and organizing protests at all 54 airports where they operate.** Our goal? Drive ticket sales to ZERO and make Avelo feel the consequences of profiting from deportations.

On May 31st, Indivisible Mesa was part of the **26 protests across the country** who came together to protest Avelo Airlines on the same day for the first time! To keep the pressure on Avelo, the Coalition is planning to support additional nationwide protests and Indivisible Mesa is again joining the call!!

**Indivisible Mesa will be protesting against Avelo Airlines operating ICE deportations on Saturday, June 28th!** 

By protesting together, everywhere, on the same day, we elevate our anti-Avelo movement from a local news story to a can't miss national news story!

🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨

The message to **Avelo** is simple: **"Cancel your contract with ICE."**

The message to **City Hall** is simple: **"Stop funding Avelo with local dollars."**

The message to **travelers** is simple: **"Boycott Avelo, don't give them your money."**

The message to **allies** is simple: **"Join us. Stand for justice. Fight inhumanity."**

And the message to the **world** is powerful: 
*We stand for families. 
We stand for immigration rights. 
We stand for due process. 
We stand for all Americans who are feeling scared and vulnerable. 
We stand against companies that sacrifice people for profit. 
We stand against blood money and we stand against deals-with-the-devil. We stand against Avelo's contract with ICE. 
And we stand together, together, together. 
We will win this fight! 
We will force Avelo to cancel its ICE contract.**

Protest locally, speak nationally.

✨Be safe, be lawful, be loud. Bring signs. Bring friends. Take pics.✨


==**Protest Information**==

🌄 Indivisible Mesa will be at the intersection of East Ray Rd and Power Rd.

🅿️ There is PLENTY of parking in the store surrounding the intersection, including Walmart, Target, etc. 

❄️Bring all the things to keep yourself cool like cooling towels, umbrellas for shade, water, etc. and feel free to bring extra for other protestors if you are able to!

🔥Indivisible Mesa leadership realizes it may be too hot for some to attend the event, but we have to be outside and as visible as possible. IT'S VITAL. **If this means you can only protest for 20 mins, then please come for 20 mins!! Everybody and every minute counts!!**


==**Signs & Graphics**==
Please create signs and graphics that are relevant to Avelo & Mesa Gateway Airport! The messaging we put on our signs can do a lot to cut right through Mesa Gateway's bureaucratic smokescreen. 

   ☑️ Call attention to Avelo Airlines separating families

   ☑️ Complicity of Mesa/Gateway airport

   ☑️ Illegal deportations without due process

   ☑️ Human trafficking

   ☑️ Rather overheat than let human trafficking continue

   ☑️ Print out large pics of ICE kidnapping people in Phoenix

Please share and bring friends to protest against these flights that are illegal, inhumane, & unconstitutional.

title: Lemon Sticks with Lawmakers
description:
🍋 Lemon Sticks with a Lawmaker 🍋
Presented by Indivisible Baltimore County at Sounds of Solidarity
June 21 | 11AM–4PM | Patterson Park, Baltimore City

Come cool off with a sweet Baltimore tradition- and a little political zest.

Join us for Lemon Sticks with a Lawmaker, where constituents and elected officials meet face-to-face in the heart of the park. It’s a chance to share the sweet and the sour- because real dialogue is how we get through the tough stuff together.

In sour times, sweeten it up with real talk and real connections- solidarity is our secret ingredient.

Bring your questions, your hopes, and your appetite for change.
🎶 Music, community, and citrus-powered conversation await!

* timing for elected officials' arrival will be dependent on individual schedules *

Thinking about running for office? Indivisible Baltimore County supports a bottom-up approach to making real change in our communities. Indivisible is a progressive movement- while we do not endorse candidates, we do endorse conversations, and this is the perfect place to make yourself heard!

For more information on Indivisible Baltimore County, visit: https://indivisible-baltimorecounty.org



More on Sounds of Solidarity:

The Free State Coalition is thrilled to invite you to be a part of the SOUNDS OF SOLIDARITY, FETE DE LA MUSIQUE, a one day celebration of International Music Day that highlights community, and collective action in support of democracy for all. This event will take place on June 21 at Patterson Park. 

The Sound of Solidarity Festival aims to:

Celebrate International Music Day by showcasing the power of music to inspire change.

Provide a platform for artists whose music promotes freedom, resistance, and joy.

Raise awareness and support for social justice causes through partnerships with non-profit organizations.

Create an inclusive community event that celebrates diversity and promotes solidarity.

Support local artists, vendors, and businesses.

We envision Sound of Solidarity- Fete de la Musique to be a powerful demonstration of what we can achieve when we come together in the spirit of solidarity. We hope you will join us in making this event a success.

title: Honk & Wave: Tell Avelo Airlines to Cancel ICE Agreement

address_lines: near the intersection of Rt. 13 and School Lane

description:
Co-hosted by 302 United and Indivisible Highlands and Beyond.

Avelo Airlines has accepted a $150 million contract to operate deportation flights, aiding and colluding with the federal government in the illegal removal of individuals without their right to a fair hearing or due process. 

We demand that Avelo Airlines cancels their agreement with ICE immediately. Come out and help us keep up the pressure on AVELO and to promote a boycott until they change course.

Bring signs! We will have some to share, but we urge you to continue making your own great/creative signs! (Given often fast-moving traffic, a reminder about signs: 
Keep the message simple;
use large letters;
and make the letters thick and bold.)

We'll rally on both sides of Rt. 13, so stay on whichever side of the highway you park on. Please do NOT cross the busy highway!

After the Honk & Wave, all are welcome to gather at the IHOP across the street for "Protest and Pancakes!" (You don't have to get pancakes; they have avocado toast and veggie sausage, too!) Join us to connect and converse!!

Parking Options:

Go to Lot D, $7.00 per car, then walk to the nearby sidewalk along the DuPont Hwy. (The first section of Lot D is a quick right turn after passing the ChristianaCare-GoHealth Urgent Care, right next to the Wilmington Airport.The second section of Lot D is a right turn immediately after you past this first turn for lot D.  There is a sign for Lot D at this turn.)

You can create an account online ahead of time so you can complete your payment from home in advance.  We recommend taking this step ahead of time, so you can just park and join us. Go to this link to set up your parking account: https://p-123.com/. Click on the ‘create your account now’ button. You will be asked for the zone ID which is 10500. You will add your license plate number, then pay with a credit card. 
You could also use this same link or a QR code once you arrive to pay.  The signs in the parking lot have this info.

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._

title: A Funeral for the Constitution - A Peaceful Protest of the Inaction of Senator Thom Tillis
description:
Join us on August 23, we will gather in downtown Greensboro dressed in black, not in celebration - but in mourning.
This solemn protest, led by concerned citizens across North Carolina, is a funeral march for our Constitution - the foundational document Senator Thom Tillis continues to undermine and nullify, piece by piece.
As we carry a symbolic coffin through the streets, accompanied by the haunting sound of a lone bagpipe, we will grieve the erosion of civil liberties, voting rights, and democratic norms. This is not a spectacle. This is a eulogy - for fairness, for accountability, and for a government of the people.

With peaceful resolve and powerful symbolism, we will honor what has been lost and demand better from those elected to serve us. We mourn, we march, and we resist - because democracy should not die in silence.

title: Get in Line, Senator Tillis
description:
This joyful protest gets in step for justice - literally.
"Joy is a form of resistance" is often attributed to the poet Toi Derricotte.

We're dancing to send a clear and unified message to Senator Thom Tillis: it's time to GET IN LINE with the people of North Carolina! While he continues to ignore the will of his constituents, we're responding not with silence, but with rhythm, joy and movement! Our feet will hit the ground in Guilford County on July 12, where every step is a stand - a stand for community building, for kindness, and for those whose voices have been sidelined.

With music, unity and purpose, we're turning this protest into a celebration and resistance into motion! Join us - because when we move together, we shift the future, and we won't stop dancing until our representatives fall in line with the people they serve!

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** 

Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: extrajudicial kidnappings have no place in our country. The USA is a nation founded on free speech, due process, and liberty. We will gather to demand the end of extrajudicial kidnappings by ICE and the Trump administration.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._

title: NO NUKES VIGIL - Every Friday
description: The Santa Fe chapter of Veterans For Peace started this vigil in 2002 and have continued it every Friday at noon for 23 years. Its purpose is to bring awareness to the hundreds of billions of our tax dollars going to the production of new nuclear weapons here in our state. Many people, even many New Mexicans, are unaware that Los Alamos National Lab is currently building several new bomb factories to increase production of nuclear bomb cores (known as plutonium "pits") to reach a goal of 30 to 120 new pits per year. Each pit, on average, has the destructive power of 20 Hiroshima-sized bombs. Loud public outcry may be able to halt this waste of federal money, or at least slow it down until we elect a saner administration. Life on Earth is at stake.

title: Save Our Libraries
description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Indivisible McHenry County is hosting a protest rally to show our opposition to the Trump administration's proposed elimination of the IMLS (Institute of Museum and Library Services), which will affect us on a local level. The rally will take place on Friday, June 20th, in front of the McHenry Public Library, 809 Front St (Rte 31), McHenry, from 3 p.m. until 5 p.m.

On June 6th, a Federal judge gave the Trump administration permission to proceed with dismantling the IMLS even though there is another lawsuit underway that is trying to save the agency through a different Federal court.

The IMLS was created and funded by Congress in 1996 for the purpose of providing support to libraries and museums in every state in the U.S. The agency has had bipartisan support throughout its history, with reauthorization occurring under the Clinton, George W. Bush, Obama, and Trump administrations. The IMLS is required by law to conduct activities that support libraries and to provide reports to Congress on important issues. The devastating cuts to the IMLS’s grants and services will make it impossible for the agency to operate as required by Congress. 

Although libraries in McHenry County do not rely on the IMLS for most of their funding, the elimination of the IMLS could still result in cuts to library services that are enjoyed by our residents and tens of thousands of other people in Illinois. The IMLS provides millions of dollars in funding to the Illinois State Library that is used to fund RAILS (Reaching Across Illinois Libraries System), the government agency that assists more than 4000 library facilities in Illinois, including all of the libraries in McHenry County.

RAILS provides the interlibrary delivery service which allows library patrons to check out books and other items from any library within the Illinois system. RAILS also provides: a shared electronic catalog and cataloging support • group purchases and member discounts that helps libraries to save money • continuing education and consulting resources to library employees and trustees • content services for online publishing • grant opportunities for local libraries • and many other valuable services. If the IMLS is eliminated it is unlikely that RAILS will be able to survive, and all of the valuable services that it provides to our residents will also be eliminated. Let your voice be heard. Please join us on June 20th.

title: Weekly (Tues) I-91 Overpass Standout - Mtn Park Rd, Holyoke, MA
description:
Come out to show that ordinary people can raise their voices against the chaos and destruction of this Administration. Help remind folks that they, too, can stand up for their beliefs - and that there's lots and lots of people who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and Musk and the GOP.

### Recent DOT Visits

A Department of Transportation employee has visited twice in the past three weeks prior to 5/20 to ask that people NOT attach anything to the fencing. On 5/20, he parked and waited until everything was removed from the fencing. It seems reasonable to expect that DOT enforcement will continue.

### How to Get There

The address "9 Mountain Park Rd, Holyoke" will get you there if you're using Waze. (Mountain Park Road runs off Route 5, and is not accessible from I-91.) People have reported that some GPS systems bring you right under the bridge, but on I-91. That’s annoying!

Please park on the side of the road before the bridge. We can't park on the bridge.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

Donations...we've purchased banners and grommets and flags and zip ties and bungee cords, and we'll be getting more. We’ve purchased 20” x 30” letter boards for messaging we can change. All this costs $$$. We'll have a bucket for donations, and if you could throw something in, that'd be great. And if not, that's perfectly OK, too - your presence is what's really important. See where the money's going! https://tinyurl.com/IN-SLWMProtestTeamFinancials

title: WE LOVE PUBLIC LANDS RALLY
description:
Mark your calendar. Please join us for a critical rally on Monday, June 23, to show our love and support for New Mexico's public lands and national monuments.



THIS IS OUR MOMENT: U.S. Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum will be in Santa Fe on June 23rd, speaking at the Western Governors Association meeting alongside three other cabinet secretaries and several governors. We must seize this opportunity to make our voices heard on the future of our cherished public lands! 



Rally Details:

Date: Monday, June 23, beginning at 3:30 pm
Meeting Point: De Vargas Park (a few blocks from the El Dorado Hotel)
What: Peaceful rally and march to the El Dorado Hotel (WGA meeting location)
Message: New Mexicans love our public lands, and we want to keep public lands in public hands! 


We need you there: Plan to bring friends, family, and anyone who cares about our public lands. Come with signs supporting public lands and national monuments. We need to organize a HUGE turnout for this peaceful rally and march. Please share far and wide!



As New Mexicans, we love our public lands and believe they belong in public hands. Our shared love for these special places unites us. Let's come together to make sure these leaders hear that message loud and clear!
More details to follow soon!

title: Mondays @ McCormick's
description:
This is an EMERGENCY! Senate Protest Event in Philadelphia Continues This Week and For the Foreseeable Future.

Now called "Monday's at McCormick's" each Monday at noon - rain or shine - Here's why:

We are living in a MAGA-republican Coup. We were warned. Now it's here!

Here at home our democratic rights are being eroded and the Trump/Musk team is putting us all in danger. The limits of Executive power against the courts are being tested every day. If Trump decides to ignore the courts, there is very little they can do to enforce their decisions and unless Congress acts, it would be a true constitutional crisis. (And so far, Congress is controlled by the MAGA movement and the Democrats have not done enough to stand up and fight back.) It could even spiral down into outright civil war as competing factions and states careen between untested solutions to protect their own interests and those of their constituents and funders. There is real harm being done across the entire domestic sector. Layoffs, program cuts for the needy and for the average US resident, persecution of law abiding immigrants and students and other activists for simply speaking their mind and organizing constitutionally protected protest. Fear is also their weapon.

Our international role is being flipped on its head - yes, the US has always had a questionable foreign policy, providing aid and promoting democracy and human rights - to a degree - on the one hand, while at the same time invading other countries for the good of corporate profits and geopolitical dominance. Trump considers a policy to outright invade counties like Mexico and Greenland in violation of international law and to extend US power - A clear expression of Empire! Trump is considering power grabs not unlike those that the Nazi regime in Germany perpetrated in search of "Lebensraum", (Living Space) a euphemism for territorial conquest. And they got away with it (for a while) because the people who stood up were either jailed, exiled or murdered. The rest were either regime supporters (Like the solid 30% base of the MAGA movement) or went along out of fear of retribution. We cannot let fear prevent us from standing up this time. History will judge us.

We now have a true oligarchy in the US and we must fight back!

The Trump administration’s illegal actions and relentless efforts to dismantle protections for vulnerable communities — both here in the U.S. and abroad— have made clear we are in the midst of an authoritarian takeover not unlike what has happened in Orban’s Hungary. 

His plan to "Own Gaza" and move out Palestinians is NOT a plan to destroy Hamas and increase Israeli security - it is ETHNIC CLEANSING pure and simple. It's a land grab. All for development rights and to secure a seaport access to natural gas deposits off the shore of Gaza in the Mediterranean Sea. The Levant gas field includes the shores of historic Palestine (Israel and Gaza), Syria, Lebanon and, on the opposite side, the island of Cyprus. This field is estimated to contain about 122 trillion cubic feet of natural gas. So it will accelerate the climate emergency. 

As we all know Trump/Musk plan to get rid of a number of government agencies that protect our health, livelihood and constitutional rights. - the EPA is on the hit list. The Department of Education is too. So, is the CDC, the NIH and many other important agencies that protect the US public.

As we all know - thousands have already been fired, causing chaos and havoc and real harm to both dedicated civil servants AND people served by life affirming programs voted on by the U.S. people and enacted, in most cases, by the U.S. Congress. The Administration may have authority to make staffing decisions, but as is the case with the Department of Education - many of these agencies can only be eliminated by acts of Congress - Trump has overstepped his legal authority.

Thankfully, the courts have, so far, acted as a check on much of Trumps clear and blatant abuses of executive power. But we cannot count on the courts, particularly the US Supreme court, which has been stacked by Trump appointees and ideologues friendly to executive power. 

Resistance is NOT futile - it is essential. 

We are launching "Monday's at McCormick's" each Monday at noon - rain or shine - we will assemble peaceably - as is our constitutional right - outside Senator McCormick's Philadelphia office until Senator McCormick agrees to meet with us and support our demands: (These will change as conditions develop)

 1 - Stop voting for legislation inspired by Trump's project 2025 agenda - a plan to slash Medicaid, gut school lunch programs, and shut down nursing homes while handing more power to billionaires like Elon Musk. 

2- Roll back Trump's mean spirited and Unconstitutional funding pauses. Shutting down USAID is already killing people in need all over the World. Cuts to programs here in the US could do the same. Funding for these programs are up to the Congress and the US people to decide, not Trump! 

That's just for starters. Overall we want Senator McCormick to represent us all, not just his rich friends. We want Senator McCormick to DO HIS JOB!
The stakes could not be higher. The administration is pushing an authoritarian agenda that threatens our democracy, our rights, and the well-being of millions here at home and around the planet. 

We have the power to resist—and we must use every tool at our disposal to stop them.

title: People over Profit: Billionaires Shouldn’t Rule America
description:
## **People over Profit: Billionaires Shouldn’t Rule America**

The United States is not a corporation, and our government is not a for-profit enterprise. Elon Musk is not a government official. He’s a billionaire with no accountability to the American people, and nobody voted for him. Our democracy deserves better.

Musk and Trump will only be defeated by a massive, bipartisan movement of everyday Americans standing up against corruption, authoritarianism, and huge tax breaks for the rich, while fighting for the programs that working people need.

** This is a BIPARTISAN, PEACEFUL Protest** 
**No violence or Destruction of Property will be tolerated** 

**The People over Profit Movement**

Right now, millions of Americans across the political divide are struggling. 60% live paycheck to paycheck, many earn very low wages, and 85 million lack proper health insurance. College is too expensive for young people, a quarter of seniors live on $15,000 a year or less, and childhood poverty is among the highest in the world. We also face a severe shortage of affordable housing.

At the same time, the wealthiest Americans, like Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, and Mark Zuckerberg, are getting richer. Since Trump’s election, their combined wealth has grown by over $200 billion—more than the bottom half of the country. Meanwhile, the middle class shrinks, and democracy is at risk.

Our goal is to protect democracy and create an economy that works for everyone, not just the rich. As the wealthiest country in the world, we have the potential to use new technologies to improve everyone’s lives, but instead, most of the wealth goes to the people who need it the least.

We must make healthcare a human right, raise wages to a living standard, improve public education, address the housing crisis, create good-paying jobs to fight climate change, and end all forms of discrimination.

**We the People believe that in the richest country in the history of the world we must establish that:**

1. Healthcare is a human right and must be available to all regardless of income.

2. Every worker in America is entitled to earn a decent income. We must raise the minimum wage to a living wage and make it easier for workers to join unions.

3. We must have the best public educational system in the world, from childcare to vocational training, to graduate school – available to all.

4. We must address the housing crisis and build the millions of units of low-income and affordable housing that we desperately need.

5. We must create millions of good paying jobs as we lead the world in combating the existential threat of climate change.

6. We must abolish all forms of bigotry.

It is a requirement of all attendees that you help uphold our commitment to non-violence and de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. 

Here are some suggestions to keep this a peaceful, civil protest: 

• Keep away from the Tesla employees, dealership, and their immediate surrounding property. Protest events at Tesla locations or other Musk properties should be focused on Elon Musk's role as a political actor and government agent. Protests should not be aimed at attacking the business interests of Tesla or their customers. 
• Stay on the sidewalk next to the public streets and keep off the lawn next to their building. 
• Stare past any agitators like they don’t exist. 
• Start a conversation about something random with someone near you. 
• Focus on music and the people driving by cheering in support. 

For your safety and the safety of those around you, consider not engaging with anyone that tries to provoke you. 

Parking and What to Bring:

• There is plenty of parking at the mall and near the Starbucks across the street from the Tesla Dealership.
• Bring a sign that expresses your feelings/what you're there for. 
• Water to stay hydrated, a sweater/coat, sunscreen, a hat, masks if you feel it necessary.
• Something to sit on if you want to attend, but cannot stand for hours on end.
• A playlist with upbeat music and a bluetooth speaker to help keep people around you positive and motivated.

“Courage is not the absence of fear, but rather the assessment that something else is more important than fear.” – Franklin D. Roosevelt 

Resist. Dissent. Persist.

title: March for Integrity (National)
description:
The [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/) is organizing a peaceful, non-partisan mass mobilization in **Washington, D.C.**, and at **all 50 state capitals**, where we expect to mobilize at least **two million Americans** to demand:

1. A Ban on Lobbyist Gifts: Prohibiting all direct or indirect financial incentives from lobbyists to members of Congress.
2. The End of Congressional Stock Trading: Preventing elected officials from using privileged information to personally benefit.
3. The Overturning of Citizens United: Eliminating unlimited corporate campaign contributions and restoring limits on political spending.
4. A Constitutional Amendment to Keep Money Out of Politics: Ensuring that future generations do not face the same corruption and undue influence in government.

These reforms are not partisan; they are essential to ensuring a government that serves the people rather than powerful special interests.

For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:

**General Visibility Rules:**

* **Distance is Key:** The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
* **"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility:** A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
* **Bridge Specifics:** Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.

**Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:**

* **Go Big:** Aim for lettering that is at least **12-24 inches tall**, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
* **Bold, Simple Fonts:** Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
* **High Contrast Colors:** This is critical!
    * **Dark letters on a light background** (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
    * **Avoid low-contrast combinations** like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
    * **Limit your color palette** to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
* **Concise Messaging:** Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
* **Material and Construction:**
    * **Sturdy materials:** Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
    * **Weatherproof:** Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
    * **Double-sided signs:** If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
* **Test Your Signs:** Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
* **Spacing (Kerning):** Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.

By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: Four Corners in Lenexa  Standing Rally
description: As citizens, we can’t let the policies and actions of the Federal Government and unelected billionaires be normalized, but we can only stop what’s going on by coming together.  A STANDING RALLY  will draw attention to the situation, encouraging our neighbors to join with us. We will rally every Saturday morning from 11 AM – 12 PM.  Stay for the full hour or come by when and for how long you can. We will peacefully line the sidewalk on all four corners of 87th Parkway and Maurer Road,  holding signs on issues that are most meaningful to us or just simply standing in support of our neighbors and our country.  If sitting is more comfortable for you, you are very welcome to bring mobility or lawn chairs!! There is room for everyone!
accessibility_notes:
Here are a couple of notes on logistics.
Please be especially mindful of parking.  For example, if you live relatively nearby, please consider walking.  If you drive, there is street parking on the residential streets to the north and also a bit further on the south.  About ½ mile down on the west, there is a large civic campus garage at 17201 W 87th St. Pkwy.  In addition, on the SE, SW, and NW sides of the intersection, there are restaurants and shops with big, but commercially owned parking lots meant for customers.  (Please note that if you become a customer, it’s fine to bring snacks to the rally that you have bought, but please take any empty snack containers back home with you, when you leave. In any case, no matter which direction you are coming from, if it is possible, please try to park before you reach the intersection to save on congestion and choose a spot as far away as you feel comfortable walking from, leaving closer spots to those who can’t walk as far.
The rally will start on the SE corner, but as more folks arrive, we will disperse to the SW, NW, and NE corners, as well.   If you cross from one side to another, please pay particular attention to cars turning right as you cross! 
 Participants should bring their own signs (if they want to hold them).  Note that sticks supporting the signs can’t be pointed at either end.  Also, in designing content for the signs, please remember that children will be present.  
Please stand only along the sidewalks parallel to the street and not on the grass.  However, also be sure to allow pedestrian access to the sidewalk and businesses.   We are not expecting issues, but keep in mind that a core principle behind our events is a commitment to nonviolent action.  Remember to de-escalate any potential confrontation with someone,  who disagrees with you. And of course, follow directions from our excellent Lenexa police, if asked.
We will not have speakers. The plan will simply be to hold the signs we have made and wave, if that feels right.  We expect that a lot of passing cars will honk back in approval! 
Finally, please note that all our organizers will be wearing lanyards with badges reading  “Standing Rally Corner Captain or “Standing Rally Media/City Liaison”.  If you see other folks with “Press” marked on their clothing or who are giving direction to you, know that they are not part of Four Corners and are not endorsed or vetted by us.
See you soon.  Let’s show our neighbors “what Democracy Looks Like”!!
P.S.  If you want to post an inspiring (!) story about your experience, please add #FourCornersinLenexa to your post!

title: Northern Vermont Stands Up for Democracy!
description: Can you hear it? The voice of WE THE PEOPLE is growing. Around the country people are waking up, showing up, and joining up with their neighbors to rally to protect our Democracy, our Constitution, and our rule of law. The energy of the Hands Off! rallies is now spreading from city centers to other Vermont small towns. Beginning May 3rd, join your friends and neighbors right in your community. (St. Albans will gather at Taylor Park, Enosburg will gather at the Lincoln Park sidewalk along Main Street, Fairfax will gather at the Fairfax Community Corner Park, Milton will gather on RT 7 in front of Hannafords) Put your own community on this list as well by encouraging your friends and family to come out in your town to Stand Up for Democracy! The organization is simple: just gather with others each Saturday in a visible spot in your community from 11:00 to noon to defend our Democracy and civil liberties! Bring your best signs, flags, and energy! These will always be family-friendly peaceful demonstrations. Organized jointly by Green Mountain Alliance Indivisible, Rail City Indivisible, Cold Hollow Indivisible, and Franklin County Vermont Women for Democracy.
